title: How to pick between two good business options: choose the one that sounds most fun to build
summary: Jason Cohen answers a founder torn between raising money and staying bootstrapped. When both options are valid, outside advice can't settle it and delay is costly, so use your own fulfillment as the tiebreaker. Ask which kind of company sounds most fun to build.

principles.text: When both options are rational, there is no wrong answer; never feel guilty for not choosing the other.
principles.quote: This is one of those few dilemmas where there's no wrong answer. So, whichever you choose, never let anyone else make you feel guilty about not choosing the other.

principles.text: Outside opinions can't settle it: critics exist on both sides, so the answer has to come from you.
principles.quote: Who's right? Both. Neither. This is why you cannot look externally for the answer.

principles.text: Dithering is costly: it drains time and energy and blocks other decisions like hiring, spending and features.
principles.quote: Dithering doesn't move you closer to either goal--it's draining time and energy, and it's blocking other decisions about spending money, hiring, your lifestyle, stories for the press, features, everything.

principles.text: Use fun and fulfillment as the tiebreaker: ask what kind of company sounds most fun to build.
principles.quote: What kind of company sounds like the most fun to build?

principles.text: Founders undervalue joy and fulfillment in the calculus, which is a mistake.
principles.quote: I think fulfillment and joy barely enter into the calculus for most founders, and that's a mistake. Why build a company--or anything else for that matter--if it's not fulfilling?

principles.text: Hindsight won't tell you which path was right, so don't expect certainty later; others can help you ask better questions but not decide.
principles.quote: five years from now when you look back on this with hindsight, you still won't know which one would have been "right."
